question.text: After Nicholas abdicated, he and his family were executed, paving the way for this Bolshevik ("BOWL-she-vick") leader to assume power.
question.clue: An online poll is asking civilians to vote whether or not to bury his body, which is presently displayed in Red Square.

swap.text: This first tsar of Russia led the unsuccessful Livonian War. He was known for his cruelty, which could be seen in his killing of his second son.
swap.answerHtml: Ivan the Terrible [or Ivan IV of Russia; or Ivan Vasilyevich; or Ivan Grozny; prompt on Ivan]
swap.clue: This ruler created his nation's first standing army, the Streltsy, as well as a secret police force called the Oprichnina.

question.leadin: The most famous events of this name are the brutal crackdown of a 1965 civil rights march in Alabamaand a 1972 massacre of Northern Irish civilians in Derry.
question.text: Give this multi-word name shared by several dozen events, typically instances of violence by soldiers orpolice against protesters.
question.clue: The first day of the Battle of Paardeberg during the Second Boer War was given this name, as was the beating of protesters by police during the Selma to Montgomery March.

swap.text: The Cossack rebel Yemelyan Pugachev claimed to be the dead husband of this "great" Empress of Russia, and launched a rebellion. He was unsuccessful.
swap.answerHtml: Catherine the Great [or Catherine II of Russia; or Yekaterina II Velikaya; or Sophie Friederike Auguste, Prinzessin von Anhalt-Zerbst]
swap.clue: This ruler's private art collection led to the founding of the Hermitage Museum.

question.leadin: Name these other people who survived assassination attempts.
question.text: This General Secretary of the Communist Party in the Soviet Union was almost killed by Soviet Army deserter Vikoty Ilyin. He was succeeded in his post by Yuri Andropov.
question.clue: His economic policies have been described as "the lowest stage of socialism," and this man is remembered for recognizing postwar European boundaries with the Helsinki Accords.

swap.text: In 2014 Russia sent troops into this peninsula on the Black Sea's northern coast, a region still claimed by Ukraine.
swap.clue: British soldiers in this region frequented the "British Hotel" of Mary Seacole during one war.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Rurikid dynasty.
question.text: The Rurikid dynasty came to an end when Ivan IV was succeeded by Boris Godunov, whose death began this period in Russian history. It was ended by Mikhail Romanov's accession.
question.clue: The eruption of a Peruvian volcano may have caused a massive famine during this period that included the Battle of Klushino.

swap.leadin: Napoleon signed a lot of treaties.
swap.text: While on a yacht in the Neman river, Napoleon signed the treaty of Tilsit with this monarch. This czar led Russia during Napoleon's conquests.
swap.clue: After his nation lost the Battle of Friedland, he met with Napoleon on a raft in the Niemen River to sign the Treaty of Tilsit.

question.text: This capital of the USSR was the site of the 1980 Olympics, as well as frequent "physical culture" parades in Red Square.
question.clue: This city traces its history to a post founded by Yuri of the Long Arm.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Greek historian Xenophon.
swap.text: According to Xenophon, the Ten Thousand cried "Thalatta! Thalatta!" after seeing this sea near the city of Trebizond, meaning they had returned to Greek city-states.
swap.clue: To defend one of its ports, Eduard Totleben ordered a fleet sunk to block the harbor, and the subsequent siege ended after the taking of Malakoff Redoubt.

question.leadin: Name these places in where news has occurred over the past few years.
question.text: International Chess Federation president Kirsan Ilyumzhinov has run this constituent as a personal dictatorship since 1995, funneling tax dollars into extravagant monuments to chess and having opposition journalists murdered.

swap.text: After an invasion of Livonia by this Russian ruler, Sweden formed a coalition with Poland and Lithuania to drive off the Russian incursion. Sweden was given modern-day Estonia from Livonia in the ensuing peace.
swap.answerHtml: Ivan IV Vasilyevich [Accept Ivan the Terrible or Ivan Grozny.]
swap.clue: Difficulties in his later years included a botched military campaign to retake western Slavic lands in the Livonian War, and the harsh government he created called the oprichnina, a far cry from his earlier Chosen Council.

question.leadin: This man married Anna, the daughter of the Byzantine emperor, in exchange for military aid.
question.text: Name this Rurikid king, the father of Yaroslav the Wise, who used Old Church Slavonic for the Eastern Orthodox rites he converted to.
question.answerHtml: Vladimir I [or Vladimir the Great or Vladimir Svyatoslavich or Vladimir Veliky or Saint Vladimir; accept Volodimir Sviatoslavych from any Ukrainians]
question.clue: Basil married his sister, Anna Porphyrogenita, to this man in return for military assistance. The Primary Chronicle is the source of an anecdote in which this man sent envoys to learn the religions of the world.

swap.leadin: After this person had him arrested, Jan Chryzostom Pasek ("yahn hree-ZO-stome PAH-sek") possibly made up a story about this person being beaten up by his neighbor after he had an affair with his wife.
swap.text: Name this Cossack hetman and Ukrainian national hero. After he learned he was about to be replaced by Alexander Menshikov, this person defected during the Battle of Poltava.
swap.clue: This Ukrainian leader sought to reunite his homeland and so he turned against his former ally, Peter I, and joined Charles XII of Sweden. He was defeated at Poltava.

question.leadin: Dissidents and political enemies of Russia have a much higher-than-average rate of being the victim of an unsolved assassination. Curious. Answer some things about those crimes.
question.text: This former FSB officer and defector to Britain fled Russia in 2000 after accusing his bosses of murdering an oligarch. Six years later, he mysteriously died of polonium poisoning after meeting with Russian agents.
question.clue: Shortly before that, he appeared in a video tape revealing other orders to kidnap and kill, and he had been arrested earlier for theft of explosives and abuse of office in Kostroma.

swap.leadin: Ulugh Muhammad founded this state as a descendant of Tugh Temur.
swap.text: Name this state whose massacre of merchants at its fair prompted the creation of the Makariev Fair. Saint Basil's Cathedral was built to celebrate the conquest of this state.
swap.clue: Massacres of resident Muskovite merchants were a recurrent feature of this polity's history, by which it eventually harmed itself when the rival Makariev Fair was founded to provide a more secure commercial environment than the one in its central city.

question.leadin: She was offered the throne by the Supreme Privy Council on the death of Peter II.
question.text: Name this Russian empress whose reign was dominated by Biron, Osterman, and Munnich, and who oversaw Russian participation in the War of the Polish Succession during her reign.
question.clue: After the Supreme Privy Council put this woman in power, she promptly abolished it.

swap.leadin: Name these advisors to Catherine the Great.
swap.text: This final lover and favorite of Catherine was of ignoble birth and irritated his courtiers by allowing his pet monkey to steal their hats. After being exiled from court by Tsar Paul following Catherine's death, he participated in the coup against Paul.

question.leadin: Russian imperialism in Central Asia is often neglected. Answer the following about it.
question.text: Russians loved fetishizing the women from this Caucasian tribe, who were often taken as concubines by Russian adventurers and generals. They were subjugated after losing their namesake war in 1864.
question.clue: A dynasty of this ethnic group, which includes the Adyghe ("ah-dih-GAY") and Kabardians, replaced the Mamluk Dynasty's Turkic Bahri dynasty.

swap.text: Though he lost at Borodino, this Russian Field General defended his nation against Napolean's invasion.
swap.clue: He once claimed that he would bury the French at Galicia, but his plan to retreat to the Carpathians was rejected and led to a crushing defeat for his allies.
